# Template: ci_dance
What "95% confidence" actually means: many repeated samples, each yielding one confidence interval, stacked as horizontal bars against the fixed dashed line of the true value — most catch it, and the expected share MISS it (drawn in red). The method is reliable; any single interval may lie. Choose this scene for ANY request about confidence intervals and their interpretation, what 95% means, repeated sampling, coverage, or why one study's interval can be wrong.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "draws": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "How many repeated-sample intervals to stack, 5-40 (default 20)."
  },
  "confidence": {
   "type": "number",
   "minimum": 0.5,
   "maximum": 0.99,
   "description": "The confidence level, 0.5-0.99 (default 0.95); sets how many intervals miss."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- true_line: the dashed vertical line at the true value
- ci_<i>: interval i (bar + center dot, a group), top to bottom, counted from 0 (ci_0 … ci_19 for 20 draws)
- caption: the tally, e.g. "19 of 20 caught the truth"
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Show what 95 percent confidence really means with repeated samples." → params: {"title":"The confidence-interval dance"}
Request: "Show how often 80 percent confidence intervals miss." → params: {"confidence":0.8,"draws":20,"title":"80% confidence, 1 in 5 wrong"}

In YAML: `template: ci_dance` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
